messages:
elaine: Heads-up: kicking off the large docs reorg today. I split the work into multiple focused PRs to keep previews fast and reviews small. Opening in waves so we can do a canary merge.

sam: drop links when the PRs are up, I9ll pick up the file-move reviews and watch for anchor churn.

elaine: PRs opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1865 (file moves), /1866 (redirect mappings), /1867 (sdk-snippets), /1868 (examples + walkthroughs), /1869 (anchor and TOC fixes). Preview hub: https://docs-preview.redwood.ai/ (click PR tab).

maria: I9m owning redirects (/1866) and the reindex checklist. Will validate coverage and produce a mapping CSV. Ping me when /1865 preview is green.

docsbot: preview built for /1865 - https://docs-preview.redwood.ai/pr-1865 - status: green, lint: 1 warning (mdx link style)

sam: noted the MDX warning. Also reminder: moves WILL change anchors. We need strict redirect coverage + an anchor-validator run before merging.

elaine: Proposed merge sequence (must apply in order):
1) /1865 file moves (canary subset first)
2) /1866 redirects (complete map)
3) /1867 sdk-snippets (update outputs & CI runner)
4) /1868 examples (content tweaks)
5) /1869 anchor/TOC fixes + final pass & search index kick-off

ajordan: Which day/time for the merge window? prefer midweek and daytime.

tim: Block set: Tue 11:00 PT. I9ll enforce branch protection requiring "docs-preview" and block merges outside the window.

alex: For the canary, can we move ~10 pages first and verify redirects+search behavior before the full merge? I can monitor search results.

sam: yes, plan: canary = 10 topic pages across API, SDK, and Quickstart. If canary looks good we proceed. If 1+ redirect fails -> label "hold/merge-block".

ci-bot: CI statuses: /1865: success, /1866: building preview, /1867: lint failed (snippet runner mismatch), /1868: success, /1869: pending

elaine: I9ll fix the snippet runner mismatch in /1867 this afternoon and re-run. Tagging @sam @maria for review after. :eyes:

sam: local pre-merge checks I run: 
```
# validate anchors and links
python tools/linkcheck.py docs/ --anchors --report=anchors.csv
# simulate search index to catch title mismatches
scripts/simulate_search_index.sh > search-sim.out
```

maria: Redirect mapping format we9re using for the validator: one JSON object per line: 
```
{"from":"/sdk/old","to":"/sdk/new","status":301}
```
I9ll add scripts/redirect_coverage.py to assert every moved path has an entry.

docsbot: preview warning: search results stale on PR preview (moved slugs still show old titles). Post-merge reindex will fix live site.

elaine: Important: do NOT run a full site reindex during the merge window. Platform will schedule the reindex as a controlled post-merge job.

sam: small nit: some TOC entries in /1865 still link to anchors that change. I9ll leave inline comments on the PR.

alex: Ops question: does the redirect layer (CDN edge) pick up mappings immediately? we should confirm TTLs so users see redirects quickly.

maria: CDN TTL is 60s for redirect config; platform will warm the CDN as part of the post-merge hook.

ci-bot: builds updated: /1865: success, /1866: success, /1867: success, /1868: success, /1869: success (preview ready)

elaine: OK - canary plan: tomorrow Tue 11:00 PT merge 10 pages from /1865 then /1866 partial mapping for those paths. Monitor 30 minutes, then continue with remaining files if all good.

jordan: I9ll join the post-merge watch rotation. If anything looks off I9ll add the "hold/merge-block" label and ping #release-war-room.

sam: starting reviews now, will post inline comments. Keep comments brief so authors can act quickly.

elaine: Appreciate it all. We9ll reconvene here once canary completes. Please keep previews green and avoid unrelated merges to main during the window. :rocket:
